content.value_statement: Agents often repeat weak strategies when past outcomes are not captured. This skill shows how to use ReasoningBank to record experience, learn patterns, and improve future decisions.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to record task outcomes as reusable ReasoningBank experiences.
Demonstrates pattern learning and pattern matching for recurring situations.
Explains strategy comparison for selecting stronger task approaches.
Covers auto-learning thresholds for continuous improvement workflows.
Shows AgentDB persistence and queries for learned patterns.
Includes metrics examples for tracking learning effectiveness.
limitations: Requires agentic-flow, AgentDB, and Node.js 18 or newer.
Examples are TypeScript-oriented and assume application integration work.
Recommendation quality depends on enough accurate experience records.
The skill is guidance only and does not include a runnable package.

use_cases.title: Improve Agent Workflows
use_cases.description: Record task outcomes and use learned patterns to recommend better strategies for future agent runs.

use_cases.title: Optimize Engineering Processes
use_cases.description: Compare approaches across repeated tasks and identify strategies that perform best in specific contexts.

use_cases.title: Persist Learning History
use_cases.description: Connect ReasoningBank with AgentDB so learned patterns survive restarts and support later queries.

prompt_templates.title: Start ReasoningBank Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add ReasoningBank to a TypeScript agent. Show the initialization steps and explain each required option.

prompt_templates.title: Record Useful Experiences
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an experience record for my code review agent. Include task type, approach, outcome metrics, and context fields.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Task Strategies
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ReasoningBank concepts to compare three debugging strategies. Recommend what data I should collect before ranking them.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Adaptive Learning
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a ReasoningBank learning loop with AgentDB persistence, pattern queries, confidence thresholds, and periodic quality review.

output_examples.input: A team wants an agent to improve code review decisions over time.
output_examples.output: The skill guides the agent to record each review outcome, capture context, compare strategies, and reuse stronger approaches later.

output_examples.input: A platform needs persistent learned patterns for repeated incident response tasks.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines AgentDB-backed storage, confidence filtering, pattern queries, and metrics for monitoring learning quality.

output_examples.input: A developer needs to choose between several task execution strategies.
output_examples.output: The skill shows how to compare strategies by task type, context, success metrics, and observed performance history.

best_practices: Record both successful and failed outcomes so recommendations reflect real performance.
Include rich task context because pattern matching depends on meaningful signals.
Review learned patterns regularly before allowing them to guide important workflows.
anti_patterns: Do not learn from low-confidence or incomplete outcomes without review.
Do not assume a strategy transfers across domains without similarity checks.
Do not keep unlimited experience history without pruning or retention rules.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps build agents that record outcomes, learn patterns, compare strategies, and improve future decisions.

faq.question: Does it include runnable code?
faq.answer: No. It provides TypeScript examples and implementation guidance for projects using agentic-flow and AgentDB.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Why use AgentDB with ReasoningBank?
faq.answer: AgentDB can persist learned experiences and patterns so agents can query them across sessions.

faq.question: How much data is needed for good recommendations?
faq.answer: The skill suggests collecting enough examples per task type and reviewing pattern quality over time.

faq.question: Can it replace human review of learned behavior?
faq.answer: No. Learned patterns should be audited, especially before they guide sensitive or high-impact workflows.
